name: Moses
description: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness

points: The child grew, and he became the son of Pharaoh's daughter. She called his name Moses, which means drawn out, because she drew him out of the water.
So Moses grew up as an Egyptian, although he was a Hebrew.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

points: Moses went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren; and he slew the Egyptian. Some of you might say Moses was a murderer; he did not kill out of hatred. What Moses did is the spirit the brothers had in the time of the Black Panthers, when racist police were killing our people; there are men locked up right now as prisoners of war from that era. We do not do that today, but that is the spirit Moses was moving in.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

points: When Moses was grown he went out unto his brethren the Israelites and looked on their burdens, and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren. Moses knew the Israelites were his brothers; he knew he was not of the Egyptian lineage and that there was something different about him.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

points: The second day two men of the Hebrews strove together, and the one doing wrong said, Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian? So Moses was out; he had to flee. You try to help our people and they will turn on you just that quick.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

points: Moses feared, and said, Surely this thing is known.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

points: When Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses; but Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Midian.

Moses gave up his whole upbringing and position. By faith he refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season. In Egypt his head was shaved, his beard cut, his dress and customs Egyptian; he laid all of it down to be what he was called to be, an Israelite.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

points: Zipporah and her family were Midianites, not Israelites; Moses married a woman of the land where he dwelt those forty years.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

points: Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law and led it to the backside of the desert, to Horeb the mountain of God; and the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush, and the bush was not consumed.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

points: Moses said unto God, Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh? This shows the humility of the forefathers: none of them sought the position they were given. The Lord chose Moses because He saw the spirit that was in him.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

points: God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you. The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob: this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.
Christ spoke to that very name: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am. He was telling them he was the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob who met Moses at the bush.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

points: Moses answered, But, behold, they will not believe me, nor hearken unto my voice. Moses knew the spirit of his people: Israel is impudent, hardhearted, and stiffnecked, a rebellious house that does not like to listen even when shown precept upon precept.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

points: The first sign: the rod cast on the ground became a serpent, and Moses fled from before it; he caught it by the tail and it became a rod in his hand.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

points: Moses said, O my Lord, I am not eloquent, but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue. Moses did not stutter, as is commonly taught; he was not fluent in the Hebrew tongue. He was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and mighty in words and in deeds, but he grew up in Pharaoh's house speaking the Egyptian language and then spent forty years in Midian, and a language moves on in forty years.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

points: Moses pressed, Send, I pray thee, by the hand of him whom thou wilt send; and the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses. Is not Aaron the Levite thy brother? I know that he can speak well; he spoke the Hebrew of the people fluently.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

points: Moses returned to Jethro his father in law and asked leave, and Jethro said, Go in peace. The LORD said, Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought thy life; the Pharaoh of chapter 2 had died.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

points: Moses took his wife and his sons and returned to the land of Egypt, and Moses took the rod of God in his hand. The LORD told him, Do all those wonders before Pharaoh which I have put in thine hand: but I will harden his heart, that he shall not let the people go.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

points: The LORD sent Aaron into the wilderness to meet Moses, and he met him in the mount of God and kissed him; Aaron believed right away. Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD and all the signs.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

points: Moses and Aaron went in and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness. That feast was the Passover.

note.label: Exodus 5: Let My People Go

points: The king of Egypt said, Wherefore do ye, Moses and Aaron, let the people from their works? get you unto your burdens. That is the standing complaint of the oppressor: the prophets are pulling the people from their labor and getting their hopes up that their God will deliver them.

note.label: Exodus 5: Let My People Go

points: Moses returned unto the LORD, and said, Lord, wherefore hast thou so evil entreated this people? why is it that thou hast sent me? For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in thy name, he hath done evil to this people; neither hast thou delivered thy people at all.

note.label: Exodus 5: Let My People Go

points: The children of Israel hearkened not unto Moses for anguish of spirit and for cruel bondage.

note.label: Exodus 6: The Promise Renewed and the Generations of Moses and Aaron

points: Moses answered, Behold, the children of Israel have not hearkened unto me; how then shall Pharaoh hear me, who am of uncircumcised lips? This is why Aaron was given him for a mouthpiece in the next chapter.

note.label: Exodus 6: The Promise Renewed and the Generations of Moses and Aaron

points: Chapter 6 is dealing with the genealogy: the families of Reuben, Simeon, and Levi, and out of Levi came Moses and Aaron. Levi begat Kohath, Kohath begat Amram, and Amram took Jochebed to wife, and she bare him Aaron and Moses.

note.label: Exodus 6: The Promise Renewed and the Generations of Moses and Aaron

points: These are that Aaron and Moses to whom the Lord said, Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt; these are they which spake to Pharaoh king of Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 6: The Promise Renewed and the Generations of Moses and Aaron

points: The Lord made Moses a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron his brother was his prophet. Moses was as God and Aaron was the mouthpiece, because Moses kept saying he was of uncircumcised lips.

note.label: Exodus 7: Aaron's Rod and the River Turned to Blood

points: It was Aaron who cast down the rod before Pharaoh, and it became a serpent. A lot of people to this day say it was Moses with the rod, because they do not read the Bible; Moses was telling Aaron what to do, and it was Aaron's rod that turned into the serpent.

note.label: Exodus 7: Aaron's Rod and the River Turned to Blood

points: So Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, Entreat the Lord that he may take away the frogs. Why did Pharaoh not call on Heqet, the god of frogs? He had to go to the Lord.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: Pharaoh said, Go sacrifice to your God in the land; but Moses answered, It is not meet, for we should sacrifice the abomination of the Egyptians before their eyes, and will they not stone us? Israel's sacrifices were the very animals Egypt held sacred, so Israel must go three days' journey into the wilderness.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: Moses warned Pharaoh, Let not Pharaoh deal deceitfully any more. The Lord removed the swarms so that there remained not one; and Pharaoh hardened his heart at this time also, and would not let the people go.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

points: Moses sprinkled ashes of the furnace toward heaven, and it became a boil breaking forth with blains upon man and upon beast throughout all the land of Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were upon the magicians themselves and upon all the Egyptians. With this sixth plague the Most High was mocking Sekhmet, the Egyptian idol goddess of health and beauty.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: Moses answered that the thunder and hail would cease, that thou mayest know how that the earth is the Lord's; but as for thee and thy servants, I know that ye will not yet fear the Lord God.

note.label: Exodus 9: Murrain, Boils, and Hail; Goshen Set Apart

points: Moses went in to Pharaoh with a staff and an ultimatum: how long wilt thou refuse to humble thyself? Let my people go, or tomorrow, in twenty four hours, the locusts come into thy coast.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: Moses answered that all would go, young and old, sons and daughters, flocks and herds, for we must hold a feast unto the Lord. The Most High loves to see Israel gathered together in unity; that is why so many feast days bring the nation together to honour him.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: When the judgment got real, Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste and confessed, I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you. Everything had been eaten by the locusts, and now he begged that this death only be taken from him.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven, and there was thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days, even darkness which may be felt. They saw not one another, neither rose any from his place.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: After three days of darkness Pharaoh called for Moses: go, serve the Lord, only let your flocks and your herds be stayed. Go, but leave all your possessions in Egypt.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: Moses answered, Thou hast spoken well, I will see thy face again no more.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

points: Hear how Moses spoke to Pharaoh. Yet will I bring one plague more upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt; afterwards he will let you go, and he shall surely thrust you out altogether. The other times the Lord hardened his heart because he wanted to show his wonderful power. Let every man borrow of his neighbour jewels of silver and gold; the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, and the man Moses was very great in the land. Remember Moses at first was dismayed: who made thee a ruler over us; he had to run when he tried to step up and defend his people. Now he came back as a hero for his people, empowered by the one true God.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh's servants and in the sight of the people; he had a good report. Israel in spiritual Egypt must deal the same way: have the respect of the people, and if people despise you, let it be because they hate God and the word you teach, not because you are in wickedness, shady dealings, deceit, or disrespect.

note.label: Exodus 11: The Death of the Firstborn Announced

points: The feast days commemorate the Most High delivering his people and bringing judgment on their enemies; that is the same pattern the feast of dedication commemorates. The people bowed the head and worshipped, and the children of Israel went and did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron.

note.label: Exodus 12: The Lord's Passover

points: The last time Pharaoh saw Moses he threatened to kill him if he ever saw his face again; now he called for Moses and Aaron by night, saying, Rise up, get you forth from among my people, go, serve the Lord as ye have said, take your flocks and your herds, and bless me also. Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm; the man who thought he could threaten the servant of the Most High had a complete change of tone.

note.label: Exodus 12: The Lord's Passover

points: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for Joseph had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

note.label: Exodus 13: By Strength of Hand the Lord Brought Us Out

points: Moses said, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever. The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace. Remember the lesson: the book of the wars of the Lord. When we came out of Egypt, this was one of the wars of the Lord.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: Moses stretched out his hand and the sea returned in his strength. All that water that had stood up as a wall came down on the Egyptians, their chariots, and their horsemen, and consumed them. All praises to the Most High for loving His children enough to save us by such a mighty salvation.

note.label: Exodus 14: The Salvation of the Lord at the Red Sea

points: Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore and saw the great work of the Lord, and the people feared the Lord and believed the Lord and His servant Moses.

note.label: Exodus 14: The Salvation of the Lord at the Red Sea

points: Then sang Moses and the children of Israel: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea. Israel sang gloriously about the destruction of the Egyptian army that chased them. God the Father and God the Son love war; when we were in our righteousness, God fought for us and we destroyed nations.

note.label: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

points: Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the Lord. The whole chapter is a song and a prophecy, speaking not only of the coming out of Egypt but in the future tense as well.

note.label: Exodus 15: The Song of Moses: The Lord Is a Man of War

points: The history up to this point: they were serving hard bondage as slaves in Egypt. Out of nowhere the Most High brought Moses to deliver them. They saw the water turn to blood throughout the land. They seen plagues drop on the Egyptians and not them. They literally witnessed the power of God show that all them Egyptian gods was nothing and that he was the one true God. God killed the firstborn of everyone who did not have the blood on the posts of their doors. They walked up out of Egypt with gold and jewelry, everything the Egyptians that was oppressing them had. The Lord split the Red Sea for them; they walked in between two waters to safety and the Egyptians got swallowed up behind them. They seen all of this miraculous power happen, and then they got to the wilderness talking about, I'm thirsty.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: The people murmured against Moses, saying, what shall we drink? He cried unto the Lord, and the Lord showed him a tree which made the waters sweet.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: After they complained, after they murmured, guess what God did? All right, here's some water. Here you go. And the whole congregation still murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: Your murmurings are not against us, but against the Lord. Moses is giving them the reality of the fact. You're complaining about how things are done; you're not murmuring against leadership, it's against God. There's a reason why protocols are put in place. Every protocol that was put in place was for a time; look at the Old Covenant, put in place until something else was to come.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: Your murmurings are not against us, but against the Lord. Moses and Aaron were nobody of themselves; complaining against the leadership the Most High sets is murmuring against the Most High Himself.

note.label: Exodus 16: Manna From Heaven and the Sabbath Proved

points: They said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. The word literally means, what is it? And Moses said, This is the bread which the Lord hath given you to eat. What they did not know yet in that moment, and what we need to understand, is that he was talking about Christ. The bread we were given to eat, the spiritual food from heaven, was talking about Christ.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

points: Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning; some hearkened not and left it, and it bred worms and stank, and Moses was wroth with them.

note.label: Exodus 16: Manna From Heaven and the Sabbath Proved

points: The people did chide with Moses and murmured, saying, Wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst? Same thing. You came to kill us, Moses? Knowing good and well that ain't it.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: At Rephidim there was no water, and the people did chide with Moses: wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst? At the first sign of trial the people jumped off the Lord's bandwagon again, the same as we do today when tribulation comes.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

points: Moses cried unto the Lord: they be almost ready to stone me. And the Lord said, smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it. The Lord yet again showed mercy.

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: Moses cried unto the Lord, What shall I do unto this people? they be almost ready to stone me. They were ready to kill the prophet over water, blaming the brother for what only the Most High controls; we have to build our faith up like Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who trusted the Lord even when trials came.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

points: The Lord stood before Moses upon the rock in Horeb; Moses smote the rock, and water came out of it in the sight of the elders of Israel.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

points: Moses stood on the top of the hill with the rod of God in his hand: when Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed. His hands were heavy, so they set a stone under him, and Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands, the one on the one side and the other on the other side, steady until the going down of the sun; and Joshua discomfited Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed. Aaron and Hur stayed up his hands until the going down of the sun. Moses was about eighty years old holding a rod above his head all day; the fathers were mighty men, stronger than we are today.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

points: Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven. Moses wrote it, and Deuteronomy 25 is that rehearsal: remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

points: Jethro the priest of Midian, Moses' father in law, heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel, and came to Moses in the wilderness with Zipporah and her two sons, Gershom and Eliezer.
Jethro is the same man called Reuel in Exodus 2: the priest of Midian whose seven daughters Moses helped at the well, and who gave Moses Zipporah his daughter. Reuel and Jethro are one person.

Exodus 2 also holds one of the color scriptures: the daughters told their father an Egyptian delivered them out of the hand of the shepherds. Moses, an Israelite, was taken for an Egyptian, because Israel looked like the Egyptians.

note.label: Exodus 18: Jethro's Counsel and Righteous Leadership

points: Moses laid all these words before the elders, and all the people answered together, all that the Lord hath spoken we will do. Right there Israel made a covenant, an agreement, with the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

points: Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel were called up to worship afar off, and Moses alone came near the Lord.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

points: Moses told the people all the words of the Lord and all the judgments, and all the people answered with one voice: All the words which the Lord hath said will we do. That was us making a verbal agreement with the Lord; we are our ancestors back on the earth again.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

points: Moses wrote all the words of the Lord, rose up early, and builded an altar under the hill with twelve pillars according to the twelve tribes of Israel; young men offered burnt offerings and peace offerings of oxen.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

points: Moses took half of the blood in basons and half he sprinkled on the altar; then he took the book of the covenant and read in the audience of the people, and they said, All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient. And he sprinkled the blood on the people: Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord hath made with you concerning all these words. This sprinkling ties in later to the book of Hebrews and its teaching on sacrifice.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

points: Paul confirms it: all our fathers were under the cloud and passed through the sea, and they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. The Corinthians Paul wrote were Israelites, for Greece was not even a power on the earth in Moses' day. It was Christ dealing with Israel in the wilderness on behalf of the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

points: Moses rose up with his minister Joshua and went up into the mount of God, leaving Aaron and Hur with the elders for any matters. A cloud covered the mount, the glory of the Lord abode upon Sinai six days, and on the seventh day he called unto Moses out of the midst of the cloud.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

points: If you have been actively listening: Moses already had the book of the covenant written before he went up. In the forty days and forty nights he came down with even more; it was never just the ten commandments.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

points: When he had made an end of communing with Moses upon mount Sinai, he gave him two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God. God literally wrote the testimony with his finger, and we know that was Christ.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

points: We are the same people who saw God use Moses to split the Red Sea right in front of us. It was not even long after; Moses said I will be right back, and the people gathered themselves unto Aaron: up, make us gods which shall go before us.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: When the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, they gathered unto Aaron: Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him. Any time deliverance did not come when Israel wanted it, the nation rebelled, and Moses and the leadership got the blame; the same spirit is against the leadership of Israel to this day.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

points: Moses besought the LORD his God: LORD, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand? Moses had compassion and stood in the middle, interceding and mediating between the people and God.

From the questions: the Lord dealt with Moses on a level where Moses could speak to him so, but the outcome stood on what was declared from the beginning; had it been his pleasure to destroy, nothing Moses said could have stayed it.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

points: Moses went down from the mount with the two tables of the testimony in his hand, written on both their sides; the tables were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, graven upon the tables.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

points: As soon as he came nigh unto the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands and brake them beneath the mount.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

points: Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought so great a sin upon them? He had left Aaron in charge, and came back to a camp deep in wickedness.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

points: Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, who is on the Lord's side? All the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him, and there fell of the people that day about 3,000 men.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

points: Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin. They had broken the first two commandments just given at Sinai: no other gods before him, and no graven image to bow down to and serve.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

points: “Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.” I ain't going to blot you out, Moses. Whoever broke my laws and disobeyed me, that's the one I'm putting to death and taking out of the book of life.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: Moses took the tabernacle and pitched it without the camp, afar off from the camp, and called it the Tabernacle of the congregation. The Lord dwelt there, and he would not sit in the midst of a camp that had corrupted itself; every one which sought the LORD went out unto the tabernacle without the camp.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

points: When Moses went out unto the tabernacle, all the people rose up and stood every man at his tent door and looked after Moses until he was gone in; and the cloudy pillar descended and stood at the door of the tabernacle, and the LORD talked with Moses, and all the people rose up and worshipped, every man in his tent door.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

points: The LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. That is not Moses looking eye to eye at the Lord; it means there was no mediator between Moses and the Lord, for Moses himself was the mediator between the Lord and the people, and the Lord spoke to him directly.
His servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle. Joshua was a true disciple, a learner, eager to stay by Moses' side and learn; the Lord knew his spirit.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

points: The Most High commanded Moses to hew, that is carve out or chisel, two tables of stone like unto the first, because Moses brake the first tables; the words were written in stone, and the Lord would write upon these tables the words that were in the first.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

points: When Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in his hand, the skin of his face shone while he talked with him, and Moses wist it not; and when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw it, they were afraid to come nigh him.

A man's wisdom maketh his face to shine. This was no ordinary wisdom Moses was getting; he was getting the utmost wisdom. In the mount the Most High held him by Him a long season, told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times and the end; he saw the beginning of the creation, the middle, and the end of these times, and that is why his face shone.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

points: Some of that wisdom Moses was commanded to hide and not declare; there is wisdom the Most High gave him that he was not to publish, that we do not even have right now.
Moses put a vail on his face until he had done speaking with the people; but when he went in before the Lord to speak with Him he took the vail off, to show respect to the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

points: They received of Moses all the offering which the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary; and the people brought yet unto him free offerings every morning.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: The wise men that wrought the work came and spake unto Moses: the people bring much more than enough for the service of the work. That shows how willing they were; it was too much.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: Moses gave commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp that neither man nor woman make any more work for the offering of the sanctuary; the people were restrained from bringing, for the stuff they had was sufficient for all the work, and too much.

note.label: Exodus 36: The Wise Hearted Build the Tabernacle

points: This is the sum of the tabernacle: a collection was taken in order to fund the building of the tabernacle and the service of building it, counted according to the commandment of Moses by the hand of Ithamar son to Aaron the priest.

note.label: Exodus 38: The Altar, the Court, and the Sum of the Offering

points: Chapter 39 is the application of the instructions of chapter 28: the holy garments for Aaron the priest, the clothes of service to do service in the holy place, made of the blue, purple, and scarlet as the Lord commanded Moses.

Moses gave the first covenant; grace and truth are the new one. Where the law of Moses required a man's own blood for certain things, there is now a mediator.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

points: We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write. What was written of him was written in the law and the prophets before ever he came.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

points: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up.

The history behind that is plain, and so is who it was for. It was Israel in the wilderness that spake against the Most High and against Moses, and Israel that was bitten, and Israel that looked and lived.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

points: Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust.

note.label: 2nd Commandment In The Last Days

points: Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust. For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.

note.label: John 5: The Pool of Bethesda and the Witness to the Son

points: For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. And Moses also wrote that we would be in the midst of idolatry in the latter days, and that tribulation would come upon us.

note.label: 2nd Commandment In The Last Days

points: "For Moses truly said unto the fathers, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear in all things," and every soul that will not hear that prophet shall be destroyed from among the people. The prophet is raised up "from among their brethren," meaning from among men, which proves Christ came through the seed of a man, not immaculate conception.

"Like unto thee," like unto Moses, means the same similarities: Moses spoke to the Most High directly, mediated between the Most High and Israel, gave the laws, was hidden as a child when the young were sought to be killed, and led Israel toward the promised land.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: Unable to beat him with the scriptures, they suborned men, bribing and inducing them to give false testimony that Stephen spoke blasphemous words against Moses and against the Most High. Stephen was not teaching them to break the laws; he was teaching them to accept Christ as the sacrifice, and they could not tell the difference between mercy and keeping the law.
The same thing was done to Paul in Acts 21, when they charged that he taught the people not to keep the customs of Moses.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

points: The false witnesses said Jesus of Nazareth would destroy the temple and change the customs Moses delivered. But Christ said He came not to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfill. The only thing set aside was the sacrifice and offerings, and even that is written throughout the old testament.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

points: In that time Moses was born, exceeding fair, nourished up in his father's house three months, and when he was cast out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and nourished him for her own son.

note.label: Acts 7: Stephen Rehearses the History and the Stiffnecked Resist the Holy Ghost

points: Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was mighty in words and in deeds. That corrects the doctrine that certain Christian pastors preach, that Moses stuttered and could not speak. You cannot be a stupid man and be a prince over Egypt. He was raised under Pharaoh, so he had to learn everything of Egypt, their gods, their laws, the language. He was not a stupid man, and he did not stutter.

note.label: Acts 7: Stephen Rehearses the History and the Stiffnecked Resist the Holy Ghost

points: Certain of us will be put in different positions in this society, in politics, in education, and the Most High will use those accolades to your advantage, the same way he used Moses to go to Pharaoh and not be put to death right off the bat. Then Moses fled and was a stranger in the land of Midian, understanding that if he stayed among his own people they would get him killed, and there he begat two sons.

note.label: Acts 7: Stephen Rehearses the History and the Stiffnecked Resist the Holy Ghost

points: This Moses, whom they refused saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge, the same did the Most High send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel that appeared in the bush. Be careful with one another; the same person you reject is the same person the Most High raises up over you. This is the spirit of preeminence, not wanting another brother to rule over you because you believe you should be in that position. The Most High sees the heart and knows the spirits he is setting up.

note.label: Acts 7: Stephen Rehearses the History and the Stiffnecked Resist the Holy Ghost

points: This is that Moses who said, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren like unto me; him shall ye hear. Stephen rehearsed all the history to bring them up to Christ, because the whole ministry throughout Acts is Christ's name preached in the place of animal sacrifice. Even as Pharisees, they knew this prophecy, so he made it plain: the prophet Moses spoke about is that Christ.

note.label: Acts 7: Stephen Rehearses the History and the Stiffnecked Resist the Holy Ghost

points: “This is that Moses, which said unto the children of Israel, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear.” Moses is speaking to the children of Israel, and the prophet raised up of their brethren is Christ. Watch what comes next.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

points: Our fathers had the tabernacle of witness in the wilderness, made according to the fashion Moses had seen, which our fathers brought in with Jesus into the possession of the Gentiles, whom the Most High drove out before their face. That Jesus is Joshua, and the Most High drove out the nations before the fathers.

note.label: Acts 7: Stephen Rehearses the History and the Stiffnecked Resist the Holy Ghost

points: And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses. That is the gospel of the kingdom: that Christ had come to give you forgiveness of your sins. Because all twelve tribes had been cut off, had been in sin, in idolatry, gone into slavery, and needed a saviour, a sacrifice, that they might be forgiven of their sins. That you could be justified in Christ, which you could not be justified under Moses.

note.label: Give Diligence

points: And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses. You could not get the kingdom if you did not circumcise after the manner of Moses. But when Christ came he did away with that and brought peace between the two. Peace between the two kingdoms, the two nations. When he did away with the law of sacrifice, he did away with that separation between the nation of Israel.

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

points: Certain men came down from Judaea teaching, except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved: return to the temple, back to sacrifice law. Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them; it was a huge argument, and it went up to Jerusalem to the apostles and elders.

There rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying that it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses: the temple sacrifice system. Peter rose up: God made choice that the Gentiles, Israel scattered among the nations, should hear the gospel by my mouth; and God put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.

The sentence: trouble not them which from among the Gentiles are turned to God, but write unto them that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood. Those were their main hang-ups; and for the rest, Moses is read in the synagogues every sabbath day, so they can learn God's laws there.

note.label: Traitors and Their Exquisite Subtlety: The Judas Iscariot Effect

points: Certain men from Judaea taught except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses ye cannot be saved, and verse five names them: the sect of the Pharisees which believed, whose livelihood was sacrificing, like the pastors today afraid that this Christ takes their money.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

points: And certain men which came down from Judaea taught the brethren, and said, Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.

Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses. Meaning what? On the eighth day you had to do a sacrifice. When you got circumcised on the eighth day, you had to do a sacrifice. Can the Gentiles, can the uncircumcision, go back in time and keep that? No. So that was the middle wall of partition between the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom, the circumcision and the uncircumcision, the Jew and the Gentile, the Jew and the Greek. That is how Christ did away with it and made them both one.

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

points: But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed. Not all the Pharisees were against Christ; you did have some that believed on him. This is the great dispute of Acts 15 over circumcising and commanding to keep the law of Moses; read the whole chapter when you get a chance.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees which believed, saying, That it was needful to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Moses.

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

points: For Moses of old time hath in every city them that preach him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath day. And the Israelites read from the laws, and the Torah, and the Tanakh. We read the writings of Moses. We read about the prophets. Why do you not, in the Christian church? Because you are not the people of the book.

note.label: 2nd Commandment In The Last Days

points: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam's transgression, who is the figure of him that was to come. Adam was a similitude of Christ, but not as the offence: Adam brought the offence and Christ brought the opposite, the free gift. If through the offence of one many be dead, paradise removed and the flood, much more the grace of God by one man, Jesus Christ, hath abounded unto many. They parallel: one brought death upon the chosen nation and one brought life upon it.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

points: First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you: the northern kingdom. Esaias is very bold, and saith, I was found of them that sought me not. How many of you were seeking the Lord in the world? You were in church on a Sunday banging a tambourine; you were doing Mother's Day last week.

note.label: The Bold and the Bashful

points: Did not Israel know? Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation. Isaiah saith, I was found of them that sought me not: the northern kingdom. But to Israel he saith, All day long I have stretched forth my hands unto a disobedient and gainsaying people: the southern kingdom's builders. This is the context of Romans 11.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

points: They were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea. The baptism is the receiving of the laws and the doing of the laws, in the faith of Christ. Moses did not dip the six hundred thousand men and all the rest into rivers; where was the water? The Lord had to provide water from a rock.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

points: The ministration of death written and engraven in stones was glorious, Moses' face shining from forty days with Christ so that Israel could not behold it; how much more glorious the ministration of the spirit, and if the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more the ministration of righteousness, because under Christ you can repent of everything. That which is done away was glorious; that which remaineth, the new covenant, is more glorious.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

points: “Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth”. Those sorcerers, witches and warlocks resisted God back then. The same demons are back on this earth, resisting this truth, fighting the word of God and fighting change. Our people want change, but they don't want to change.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: Moses sprinkled the book and all the people with blood and water, scarlet wool and hyssop, the purification with blood, and almost all things are purged with blood: almost, because no animal could be offered for idolatry, bestiality, murder, adultery or Sabbath breaking, and without shedding of blood is no remission. Remission is your sin put on pause, like cancer, because the scapegoat died in your stead.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

points: By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter; choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God. Understand: in ancient Egypt, everybody was not bad off. Things were not bad for Moses; Moses made things bad for himself by killing the Egyptian.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

points: Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee. But these speak evil of those things which they know not: what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves.
